title: `compvalues -v` with no value on the line: zsh returns 0 and empties the assoc, zshrs returned 1 and left the old contents

spec.completer:
#compdef fzc0000
typeset -A va; va=(stale 1)
compvalues -i -s , hdr "aa[one]" "bb[two]"
compvalues -v va; local r=$?
compadd -U -Q -J p -X probe -- "v=$r" "va=${(kv)va}" zz

observed.measured: 2026-10-28, target/debug/zshrs built from 7b4e4af21b plus the cv_parse_word fix (zshrs 0.13.56, 134043080 bytes, sha256 5b74da8ced9d7aba) vs zsh 5.9.2, scripts/compsys_spec_fuzz.py --replay
observed.notes: cv_parse_word always allocates the value list (Src/Zle/computil.c:3388 `state.vals = (LinkList) znewlinklist();`), so bin_compvalues -v (c:3685 `if (cv_laststate.vals)`) takes the sethparam branch even when the list is empty: status 0 and the caller's assoc replaced by an empty one. The port stored None for an empty list and fell to `return 1`, leaving `va=(stale 1)` in place.

observed_when_diverging.recorded_under: copy of target/debug/zshrs at db058fbede before the fix (zshrs 0.13.56, 133988872 bytes, sha256 358b8bcef8cf2bed)

guard_verified.note: compsys_spec_fuzz --replay of this cell: FAIL on the pre-fix build, PASS on the fixed one.

why_this_fixture_exists: Found by driving compvalues directly from a completer and adding each subcommand's status and output as matches; _values itself ignores the -v status and always passes a fresh local assoc, so no generated _values spec can reach this.

controls.note: same completer with `aa,` already on the line: the list is non-empty on both sides and both shells agree (v=0, va=aa).
